from.place: Proof paragraph 2 of prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint, main-20261015: coherent finite-level mapping-complex adjunction before R lim. Supporting the graph adjunction in fixed-object enriched rectification: Corollary A.5.4 and Lemma A.5.5, printed pp. 93-94; Theorem A.5.3 provides the pointwise functor-category calculation.

proof.text: Let $p:\mathcal V^\otimes\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ be the monoidal cocartesian fibration of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category]. Here $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ denotes the nerve $N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$, exactly as in that current definition; its Segal equivalences are induced by the inert transports $\rho_i$. The algebra definition in [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability] makes $\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal M}(\mathcal V)$ the full subcategory of $\mathcal F=\operatorname{Fun}_{\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}(\mathcal M,\mathcal V^\otimes)$ on inert-preserving functors. Apply [lem-coef-cocartesian-section-colimits] with $K=\Delta^0$: every fiber has one-object colimits and every transport preserves them. A one-object cocone is colimiting precisely when its sole edge is an equivalence (the colimit criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] says precomposition is an equivalence on all mapping spaces). Thus a transformation in $\mathcal F$ is invertible exactly when each of its components is invertible in its fiber. For $x\in\mathcal M_{[n]}$, choose its inert projections $e_i:x\to c_i$ over $\rho_i$. For an algebra map $f:A\to A\prime$, naturality gives the coherent squares $f_{c_i}A(e_i)\simeq A\prime(e_i)f_x$. Both horizontal edges are cocartesian, because $A$ and $A\prime$ are algebras. Their identifications $\rho_{i,!}A(x)\simeq A(c_i)$ and $\rho_{i,!}A\prime(x)\simeq A\prime(c_i)$ therefore identify $\rho_{i,!}(f_x)$ with $f_{c_i}$ up to these equivalences. Consequently the target Segal equivalence sends $f_x$ to the tuple of the $f_{c_i}$ under these identifications. A tuple is invertible exactly when each entry is: its inverses and inverse witnesses are taken coordinatewise. At $n=0$ the target fiber is terminal and every component is invertible. Hence equivalence on all colors implies equivalence at all $x$, hence in $\mathcal F$ and in its full algebra subcategory. The converse follows by applying evaluation to an inverse. This proves conservativity of $U_{\mathcal M}$.

source.place: Lemma A.5.5, with the singleton case of Theorem A.5.3 and the target Segal equivalences.

proof.text: Fix a small sifted $K$. By [lem-coef-infinity-sifted-colimit-calculus], it is weakly contractible. The definition in [def-coef-complete-algebroid] gives all small colimits in $\mathcal V$ and their separate preservation by tensor. By [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], the fibers $\mathcal V^\otimes_{[n]}\simeq\mathcal V^n$ have $K$-colimits coordinatewise. Apply the bifunctor clause of the sifted-calculus lemma to tensor: it preserves simultaneous $K$-colimits. Inducting on $r\geq1$, the $r$-fold tensor does too: the case $r=1$ is the identity. For $r+1$, first apply $(X_1,\ldots,X_{r+1})\mapsto(X_1\otimes\cdots\otimes X_r,X_{r+1})$. The induction hypothesis and the pointwise product-colimit criterion show that this functor preserves the given colimit cocone in $\mathcal V^2$. Binary tensor then preserves it by the bifunctor clause. The associativity identifications of the monoidal structure identify this composite with the $(r+1)$-fold tensor. For $r=0$ the operation is constant at $\mathbf1$; the weak-contractibility clause of [lem-coef-infinity-coslice-colimit-formula] says the identity constant cocone is colimiting. For $\phi:[n]\to[m]$ opposite to $\theta:[m]\to[n]$, the $j$th coordinate of $\phi_!$ tensors the block $X_{\theta(j-1)+1},\ldots,X_{\theta(j)}$; an empty block gives $\mathbf1$, and coordinates outside these blocks are discarded. To verify the block formula, factor $\rho_j\phi$ as the inert map $[n]\to[r]$ opposite to $a\mapsto\theta(j-1)+a$, followed by the active map $[r]\to[1]$, where $r=\theta(j)-\theta(j-1)$. The first transport selects the block and the second tensors it, by [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category]; composition of transports is supplied by [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] with diagram shape $\Delta^0$. Every block therefore preserves $K$-colimits, including its nullary case, so every transport $\phi_!$ preserves $K$-colimits.

source.place: Lemma A.5.1; HTT Proposition 5.5.8.6 for tensor and Corollary 4.4.4.9 for empty blocks.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-cocartesian-section-colimits] to $p$, $g:\mathcal M\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, this $K$, and the specified set of inert edges of $\mathcal M$. Step 2 verifies exactly its fiber-existence and transport-preservation hypotheses. It gives a colimit $L$ of $B$ in $\mathcal F$, computed in each fiber. Its closure clause implies that $L$ sends every inert edge to a cocartesian edge, so $L$ is an algebra by [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability]. The ambient colimit cocone is also colimiting in the full algebra subcategory: for any algebra $C$, fullness identifies both its mapping space from $L$ and its mapping spaces from $B_k$ with the ambient ones, so the same colimit mapping-space equivalence applies. At a color $c$, the section theorem evaluates this actual cocone to a colimit in $\mathcal V$. Thus $L(c)\simeq\operatorname{colim}_k B_k(c)$ with its canonical cocone. The pointwise functor-category clause of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] now identifies $U_{\mathcal M}L$ with the colimit of $U_{\mathcal M}B$.

source.place: Corollary A.5.4 (i)-(iii), obtained from Theorem A.5.3, and the algebra part of (iv).

proof.text: For any algebra cocone $B\Rightarrow A$, the colimit cocone $B\Rightarrow L$ of step 3 gives a comparison $q:L\to A$ compatible with the cocones. If the cocone to $A$ is colimiting at every color, then $q(c)$ is an equivalence because both its source and target cocones are colimits of the same color diagram. Step 1 makes $q$ an equivalence of algebras; hence the cocone to $A$ is colimiting. Conversely, if it is colimiting, $q$ is an equivalence of algebras and step 3 makes every color cocone colimiting. This proves detection, and step 3 already proves preservation.

source.place: Corollary A.5.4 (iv)-(v), restricted to algebra cocones; comparison with the constructed colimit.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-infinity-sifted-colimit-calculus], $N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ is sifted in the required infinity-categorical sense. Substitute it for $K$ in steps 2-4. Thus every geometric realization exists, its color at $c$ is $\operatorname{colim}_{[n]\in\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}B_n(c)$, and its colimit cocones are detected at every color.

title: Colorwise detection of equivalences and sifted colimits of operadic algebras
statement:
Use the universes and monoidal infinity-categories of [def-coef-complete-algebroid] and the generalized nonsymmetric operads and their algebras of [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability]. Let $\mathcal M\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ be a small generalized nonsymmetric infinity operad, and let $\mathcal V$ be a presentably monoidal infinity-category. Write $U_{\mathcal M}:\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal M}(\mathcal V)\to\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal M_{[1]},\mathcal V)$ for restriction to colors. A morphism of $\mathcal M$-algebras is an equivalence if and only if its value at every color is an equivalence. Let $K$ be any small sifted infinity-category, meaning that $K$-indexed colimits of spaces commute with finite products. For every diagram $B:K\to\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal M}(\mathcal V)$ its colimit exists and is computed on each color $c$ by
$$ (\operatorname*{colim}_{k\in K}B_k)(c)\simeq\operatorname*{colim}_{k\in K}B_k(c). $$
A cocone of algebras is a colimit cocone if and only if it is one at every color. Thus $U_{\mathcal M}$ preserves and detects small sifted colimits. These assertions apply in particular to geometric realizations, indexed by $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$.

Five steps prove conservativity using the singleton section theorem, verify every monoidal transport including nullary blocks, construct colimits in the inert-preserving full subcategory, detect arbitrary sifted cocones by their comparison with the constructed colimit, and specialize to geometric realizations. Added two general, non-operadic prerequisite nodes; no item clause is moved to a child. Landing-return repair: revalidated the current monoidal definition, made its nerve-base and inert-induced Segal conventions explicit in step 1, and refreshed the verbatim step citations. The stronger relative mapping-space clause and the lax/strong functor clauses are not needed by this argument. Independent final second reading made the inert naturality squares and the product-valued tensor-induction step explicit; added new independent searches and the required second-reading audit.
